subject: Money
title: Estate Tax
description: A micro-lesson that makes Estate Tax usable.

hook.text: The Walton family fortune is $250 billion. Without estate tax, it passes to the next generation intact. A dynasty.

buildup.text: Estate tax takes a portion of wealth at death. The U.S. exempts the first $13 million; the rest is taxed at 40%.

discovery.text: Andrew Carnegie called inherited wealth a curse. Teddy Roosevelt pushed estate tax to prevent aristocracy.

twist.text: Trusts, foundations, and loopholes reduce effective estate tax to near zero for the wealthiest families.

climax.text: Without estate tax, wealth compounds across generations. Meritocracy gives way to inheritance as the primary path.

punchline.text: Born rich. Stay rich. Pass it on.

quiz.question: Why did Teddy Roosevelt support estate tax?
options: To prevent aristocracy from inherited wealth
